topics.topic: Source and ownership of the release-fixed listener addresses supplied to instance_lifecycle
questions: Which module or capability supplies the release-fixed address of each listener to `instance_lifecycle`?

Where are the two listener addresses declared, and which capability supplies them to `instance_lifecycle`? `release_declarations` offers no listener-address declaration, while configuration is stated to contain exactly its listed items.

quotes: `module:instance_lifecycle` binds the listener of each surface, at the addresses the release fixes, and accepts nothing on them yet; a listener that cannot be bound stops the start with a diagnostic naming the surface, and a listener already bound is closed.

What a release declares and a running instance reads from it alone: A22 — the artifact types with their owner services, the first release's one type (`estimate`, PresuPro) — A09 rule 2's table of the services, their operations and their highest classes; the store version; the store's temporary-name suffix (A17 rule 5); the kept and temporary backup prefixes, neither beginning with the other (A18 rule 5); the import file's size limit (A19 rule 4, its value State 6's); the release's own version and its contract version: every audit entry names both (M09), a backup's record the release (A18 rule 1).

It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).
judgement.divergence: One implementer hard-codes listener addresses in `instance_lifecycle`; another obtains them from an undeclared release or host source, so the owner and network callers observe different bind addresses and reachability.
judgement.why: State 4 requires release-fixed addresses, but neither the declared release capabilities nor the exhaustive configuration supplies them or assigns ownership of them.

topics.topic: Agent-session capability that performs registration-only validation for pointer withdrawal
questions: Which `agent_sessions` capability checks only that the session is registered, without treating the withdrawal as an operation that names no project and therefore substituting the active project?

quotes: A refusal at stage (1) or (2) records nothing and reaches no module of stages (3) to (6); the one lookup stage (2) makes of another module is a withdrawal's pointer, resolved to its project after the session is found registered (A08 rule 7, `flow:publish_and_withdraw_pointer`).

For Kernel, stage (2) first finds the session registered — an unregistered one is refused before any pointer is looked up — then `module:operations` finds the pointer's project with `capability:artifact_pointers.project_of_pointer` and `capability:agent_sessions.check_agent_call` checks that project against the set; for the owner the project is found the same way; a pointer that does not exist or whose project is outside the set is answered as not found (A08 rule 7).

For every later Kernel call, in the call's transaction, `capability:agent_sessions.check_agent_call` checks that the session is registered and, for an operation on a project, that the project named — or the active one when none is named — is in its set (A10 rules 1, 2, 5).

Candidate public capabilities

```text
register_session
end_session
check_agent_call
grant_project
revoke_project
set_active_project
request_project_access
answer_access_request
drop_project_from_sessions
read_session_access
list_sessions
```
judgement.divergence: One implementer uses `check_agent_call` before pointer resolution as a no-project call and therefore substitutes the active project, refusing a session with none active; another adds an unstated registration-only operation and then checks the resolved pointer project, so the agent and owner observe whether the pointer is withdrawn.
judgement.why: The flow requires a registration-only check before pointer lookup, but State 3 offers no capability whose stated behavior performs only that check without applying the no-project active-project rule.

witness.initial: A registered Kernel session is granted project P, has no active project, and published pointer X belongs to P.
events: `operations` must verify registration before looking up X's project.
After resolving X, Registry must check that P is in the session's set.
outcomes: Treating the initial call to `check_agent_call` as an operation naming no project substitutes the absent active project and refuses the withdrawal.
Using a registration-only check first permits X to be resolved, confirms P is granted and withdraws X.
witness.observer: The agent sees either a not-found refusal or the withdrawn pointer, and the owner sees X's status.
basis: Cabinet Kernel, for the agent, publishes an artifact pointer on a project its session is granted or withdraws one; the owner does the same in the owner interface (A08 rule 1, R0-88).
A withdrawal names the pointer only; its project is the pointer's own, and for Kernel that project is checked against the session's set (A10).
